data.title: NASA confirms Voyager 1 probe's 'light-day' distance milestone
data.description:
Key points:
  • NASA says radio signal from probe confirmed its location
  • A light-day is about 16 billion miles (26 billion km)
  • Voyager 1 probe is the most distant human-made object

By Will Dunham

NASA confirmed on Thursday that its Voyager 1 probe has achieved an unprecedented distance milestone — the first spacecraft to travel beyond a light-day from Earth — while flying into an uncertain future in interstellar space.

The US space agency said it received a radio signal from the robotic explorer, launched in 1977, indicating that it passed the distance that light travels in 24 hours — about 16 billion miles (26 billion km) — as expected on Wednesday at 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT). Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object.

NASA waited a day to make the official announcement because it took about that long for the spacecraft's signal to reach Earth.

"Traveling a light-day is a singular feat for a spacecraft, but Voyager is so much more than a distant traveler. The Voyager mission would be remarkable just for what it contributed to planetary science with the Grand Tour of the outer planets," Joe Westlake, director of NASA's heliophysics division, said in a statement released by the agency.

"But it went on to become central to NASA's fleet of heliophysics missions offering insights into the star that we all revolve around, the sun," Westlake said.

Voyager 1 journeyed past Jupiter and Saturn, the solar system's two largest planets, earlier in its mission. It continues to gather scientific data.

Voyager 1 is flying at almost 38,000 miles per hour (61,000 kph). It crossed the outer edge of the heliosphere, a protective bubble of particles and magnetic fields produced by the sun, to enter ‌interstellar space ⁠in 2012. Its twin, Voyager 2, was also launched in 1977 and entered interstellar space in 2018.

A representative at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory said this week that recent power-saving measures could give the two Voyager spacecraft enough power to stay in communication with Earth for three to four more years.

Voyager 1 is still collecting data in the near-vacuum of interstellar space on effects from the sun such as solar storms that cause shocks and pressure fronts that extend as far away as the probe's current location. The 50th anniversary of its launch is next year.

data.title: Why the VDY ETF Remains a Great Option for Dividend Investors Despite Its Gains This Year
data.description:
If you are looking for a reliable way to generate recurring income while still capturing solid gains, the Vanguard FTSE Canadian High Dividend Yield Index ETF is hard to ignore. The fund has been outperforming the broader market this year, climbing 21% year to date as investors flock to dividend stocks for safety.

One trade-off of such a strong rally is that the fund’s yield has come down. Because buyers are paying more money for the same dividend income, the yield naturally drops. Even so, at around 3%, it still offers an above-average payout that can provide steady cash flow for your portfolio.

The ETF holds 58 stocks, though it is not as broadly diversified as some other dividend funds. Because it targets high-yielding Canadian companies, financial stocks account for roughly 60% of its holdings, while energy stocks make up another 28%. Together, those two sectors represent close to 90% of the portfolio.

Given that financials and energy are home to some of the highest-yielding companies on the TSX, that heavy tilt should come as no surprise. Its top four holdings are Royal Bank of Canada, Toronto-Dominion Bank, Bank of Montreal, and Bank of Nova Scotia. Since Canada’s big banks have performed well in recent years and look a bit expensive, there is some room for a short-term pullback.

The silver lining, however, is that these banks are ultra-safe when it comes to dividends. If heavy exposure to them is the biggest knock on VDY, it remains a great long-term option to buy and hold.

data.title: Voltas signs JV agreement with Atomberg for room AC compressors, to acquire 50% stake
data.description:
Voltas has signed a definitive joint venture agreement with Atomberg Innovation Private Limited to set up a venture in India for the development, manufacture and commercialisation of room air-conditioner (AC) compressors and related parts. Under the agreement, Voltas will acquire a 50% stake in Atomberg Airtech Private Limited, an existing wholly owned subsidiary of Atomberg Innovation, upon completion of the transaction.

The agreement was executed on November 19, following the binding term sheet approved by Voltas' board on August 14, 2026. The proposed joint venture will have equal shareholding between Voltas and Atomberg Innovation, with each holding 50% of the equity.

Voltas will have the right to control the composition of the joint venture's board of directors. It will be entitled to nominate four directors, while Atomberg Innovation will have the right to nominate one director.

Following the completion of the transaction, Atomberg Airtech will become a subsidiary of Voltas. The company has also proposed changing the name of the joint venture entity after the closing of the transaction.

Voltas-Atomberg JV: Funding commitment and board structure

Under the agreement, both parties will have equal ownership in the joint venture, with a maximum funding commitment of ₹100 crore each. The capital will be infused in tranches from time to time, on terms to be decided by the joint venture entity's board.

The joint venture agreement also lays down the rights and obligations of both parties, covering board governance, reserved matters, management, business operations and funding requirements.

Other provisions include non-compete obligations and shareholding-related arrangements, such as the right of first refusal and tag-along rights. These provisions form part of the agreement governing the proposed joint venture.

Voltas currently does not hold any shareholding in any of the parties to the joint venture agreement. The company has also clarified that the parties are not related to Voltas or its promoter group and that the transaction does not constitute a related-party transaction. It has further stated that no potential conflict of interest will arise from the arrangement.

Closing subject to fulfilment of conditions

Although Voltas and Atomberg Innovation have executed the definitive agreement, the transaction has not yet been completed. The acquisition of the 50% stake in Atomberg Airtech will take place upon closing, subject to the satisfactory fulfilment of the conditions precedent specified in the joint venture agreement.

The proposed arrangement is aimed at establishing a joint venture in India focused on room AC compressors and related components, with both companies sharing ownership and funding responsibilities.

Voltas shares closed at ₹1,237 on the NSE, up ₹102.40 or 9.03%.
